claims.text: Tier 1 (deterministic, no LLM, the rigorous core): For each task, take the distilled ``semantic_slice`` and measure * recall = fraction of ``must_include`` found in the slice text, * compression = 1 - slice_tokens / whole_repo_tokens. Aggregated PER LABEL-PROVENANCE TIER (see ``daedalus.eval.tasks`` docstring) -- never blended into one number, because "hand_reachable" labels were picked by reading the code and verified reachable by the very slicer being graded (circular), while "independent_diff"/"temporal_churn" labels are not. Blending would re-hide exactly the circularity this module exists to expose. ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are excluded from every headline and reported separately (see ``run_tier1``). Any task with recall < 1.0 is a *slice-recall miss*; we surface exactly which symbols were dropped -- that is the feedback signal the structcore team uses to sharpen slices.
claims.why: The chunk contains `eval_task_tier1` which computes recall and compression, and `_tier1_aggregate` which aggregates per provenance/tier. However, the actual aggregation and exclusion logic for quarantine tasks is in `run_tier1` which is incomplete (only header shown). The claim about never blending and reporting separately cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Arms A/B/C (deterministic, no LLM -- same honesty rules as Tier 1): A/B/C is a three-way, model-free comparison of the distilled slice (A) against a naive whole-repo concat (B) and a BM25 top-k retrieval baseline (C), scored on BOTH recall (via ``_recall``) and true token cost. See ``run_arms``. This is the "does distillation actually beat dumb retrieval" question -- if C ties or beats A on some task, that is reported loudly, not smoothed over.
claims.why: No code for `run_arms` or arms-related functions is present in this chunk. The claim references `_recall` which is defined here, but the overall arms comparison is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: Tier 2 (opt-in, needs a runtime): Ask each task's question against context A (the distilled slice) and context B (whole-repo concat), score with ``answer_contains``, and compare success/tokens. Gated: if no provider is reachable it is skipped cleanly with a message -- Tier 2 NEVER crashes Tier 1 and NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled.
claims.why: No code for Tier 2 is present in this chunk. No functions or classes related to Tier 2 are defined here.

claims.text: Gate (advisory, local-only): ``run_gate`` replays the corpus against a stored ``baseline.json`` and flags PRIMARY-tier tasks whose recall decreased -- see its docstring for the exact workflow. ADVISORY ONLY: never wired to block an autonomous action; there is no CI in this repo, this is a developer-run local check.
claims.why: No code for `run_gate` is present in this chunk. The claim about baseline comparison cannot be verified here.

claims.text: The hardcoded ``TASKS`` plus every task persisted in the mint store (``daedalus.eval.mint.load_minted_tasks``) -- the load path that closes the mint -> quarantine -> confirm -> primary flywheel described in ``daedalus.eval.tasks``'s module docstring. Byte-identical to ``TASKS`` alone until something has actually been minted AND persisted: no store file -> ``load_minted_tasks`` returns ``[]`` -> this is exactly ``TASKS``, same order, same content. This is the default every ``run_*``/``*_baseline`` function below uses in place of ``TASKS`` -- additive, not a behavior change for any caller who has never run a mint.
claims.why: The function `all_tasks` returns `TASKS + load_minted_tasks()`. The docstring's description matches this implementation. The claim about `load_minted_tasks` returning `[]` when no store exists is uncheckable (depends on that function), but the additive behavior is confirmed.

claims.text: Fail-closed: only the EXACT string "primary" counts. A missing, typo'd, or otherwise unrecognized tier is treated as quarantine (excluded from any go/no-go number) rather than silently trusted -- same "never under-escalate" posture the rest of this repo uses for safety classification.
claims.why: The function returns `label_tier == "primary"`. This is an exact string comparison; any other value (missing, typo, etc.) returns False, thus treated as non-primary (quarantine).

claims.text: {provenance: {"primary": [...], "quarantine": [...]}} for every provenance actually present in ``rows``. Both tier buckets always exist (possibly empty) so a report renders a stable shape even when a task set happens to have zero quarantine (or zero primary) rows for a provenance.
claims.why: The function initializes `out[prov] = {"primary": [], "quarantine": []}` for each provenance, then populates based on `_is_primary_tier`. Both keys always exist per provenance.

claims.text: Apply ``aggregate_fn`` within each (provenance, tier) bucket. This is the ONLY aggregation path Tier 1 and the arms comparison use -- there is deliberately no top-level blended mean anywhere in this module.
claims.why: The function groups rows by provenance and tier, then applies aggregate_fn to each bucket. No blended mean is computed. The claim about arms comparison is uncheckable (no arms code here), but for Tier 1 it is correct.

claims.text: CALLERS MUST PRE-FILTER OUT ERRORED ROWS (``"error" in row``) AND FOCUS-WITHHELD ROWS (``row.get("focus_withheld")``) before passing ``rows`` here -- see ``run_tier1``/``run_arms``. Neither carries a recall/compression measurement, so folding either in would either KeyError or (worse) silently get treated as a zero, corrupting the mean it was supposed to be excluded from.
claims.why: The docstring warns callers, but this chunk does not contain the callers (`run_tier1` is incomplete, `run_arms` absent). The statement about KeyError or zero is a design note; not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Shared shape for a per-task RESOLUTION failure -- ``ValueError`` (unindexable target, e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file was renamed/deleted after minting, or an unresolvable ``repo`` label) or ``OSError`` (repo unreadable). Used by every ``eval_task_*``/``run_*`` per-task try block so one malformed task degrades to a single reported row instead of crashing the whole eval run -- "a quarantined flywheel task must not be able to take down the go/no-go machinery."
claims.why: The function returns a dict with keys `id`, `project`, `target`, `error`, `label_provenance`, `label_tier`. It catches `ValueError` and `OSError` in `eval_task_tier1` (line after the docstring). The docstring's description of the error row shape matches the code.

claims.text: ``error`` is the marker every downstream aggregator/report checks (``"error" in row`` or ``row.get("error")``). There is deliberately no ``recall``/``compression`` (or arms ``recall_A``/``tokens_A``/...) key at all -- ABSENT, not ``None`` -- so any aggregation path that forgets to filter on ``error`` fails loudly (``KeyError``) instead of silently averaging in a placeholder.
claims.why: The returned dict does not include `recall`, `compression`, or any arms keys. Only `error` is present. The docstring's claim about absence is verified.

claims.text: Shared shape for a task that is NOT scorable by slice recall. A FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS task (see ``daedalus.eval.tasks``'s docstring and ``daedalus.eval.correctness``) grades a CHANGE by running tests. It carries no ``must_include``, so handing it to ``_recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0 -- a task that cannot fail, inflating the go/no-go number with a measurement that never happened. That is the precise failure the tier machinery exists to prevent, so it is refused here rather than averaged in. Refused as an ERRORED row (``error`` key present, no ``recall``/``compression`` key at all) so it takes every existing path for a degraded measurement: excluded from all aggregates, listed in ``errored``, never silently dropped, and LOUD in ``run_gate`` when its tier is primary.
claims.why: The function returns `_task_error_row(task, ValueError(...))` with an additional `correctness_task` key. The error row has no recall/compression. The docstring's description matches the implementation.

claims.text: True iff ``semantic_slice`` fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file (see slice.py's FOCUS GATE): the withheld block contains a role=="focus" entry -- the exact shape slice.py emits when the unconditional secret floor fires on the target itself, not on some neighbour it dropped.
claims.why: The function checks `any(w.get("role") == "focus" for w in (res.get("withheld") or []))`. This matches the described condition. The claim about slice.py's behavior is uncheckable, but the function logic is correct.

claims.text: Shared shape for a FOCUS-WITHHELD row -- the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file, a lane A1 label-hygiene case distinct from ``_task_error_row``: ``semantic_slice`` did not raise (this is not a resolution failure), it legitimately returned an empty, gate-refused slice. There is NO recall/compression/missed (Tier 1) or recall_A/tokens_A/... (arms) key at all -- ABSENT, not a zero -- same "any aggregator that forgets to filter fails loudly" contract as the ``error`` marker, keyed here on ``focus_withheld`` instead.
claims.why: The returned dict includes `focus_withheld: True` and no recall/compression keys. The docstring accurately describes the absence of those keys.

claims.text: Fraction of ``must_include`` found (substring) in ``slice_text``, plus the list of items that were missed. Empty label list -> recall 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: The function returns `1.0, []` if `not must_include`. Otherwise it computes `found/len(must_include)` and the missed list. The substring check is `if m not in slice_text`, which is a substring check (exact match of the string).

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure -- ``semantic_slice``/``resolve_task_repo`` raising ``ValueError`` (e.g. the task's ``target`` is not in the index, the live repro that motivated this: a minted quarantine task whose target file had moved), or ``OSError`` reading the repo -- is caught and returned as an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating. See ``run_tier1``/``run_gate`` for how ERRORED rows are aggregated (excluded), reported (never silently dropped) and gated (primary tier fails loudly, quarantine tier is reported-only). A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced -- see ``_correctness_task_row``.
claims.why: The function catches `ValueError` and `OSError` and returns `_task_error_row`. It also checks `is_correctness_task` first and returns `_correctness_task_row`. The function never raises an exception (assuming `semantic_slice` and `resolve_task_repo` only raise those two exceptions; if they raise something else, it would propagate). The docstring claim about not raising is verified for the specified exception types.
